explanation: The V32I mutation introduces an additional methyl group (approximately 27 Å³ volume increase) into the S2/S2' subpocket where it makes direct contact with atazanavir at 4.1 Å distance, creating a steric clash that destabilizes the inhibitor's binding pose without compensatory interactions (no charge or significant hydrophobicity gain). This rigid geometric incompatibility forces atazanavir into a suboptimal conformation or partially out of the binding pocket, reducing favorable van der Waals contacts and weakening overall binding affinity by approximately 0.14 kcal/mol. The effect is modest because the mutation is somewhat peripheral (10.7 Å from ligand centroid), but the direct contact at close range is sufficient to impose enough steric strain to confer resistance.
